items.prose: A study has 1,260 daily bars. It holds out the last 252. Its rule holds each trade 5 days, so it drops a gap of 5 bars.
items.question: How many bars does research keep?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Subtract the held-out year and the gap once each.

byKey.both: The gap is dropped once, between research and the held-out year.

explain.text: $1260 - 252 - 5 = 1003$. The gap is as long as the rule's reach, so no research trade is scored on a held-out bar.

items.prose: A colleague holds out a random 20% of days, spread over all five years, so the test "sees every regime".
items.question: What is wrong with it for a 2-day momentum rule?

options.text: Test days sit beside research days, and the rule's lookback reads across them
20% is too small a share to hold out
options.why: The share is not the issue. Random days leak through their neighbours whatever the share.

options.text: Nothing: seeing every regime makes the test fairer
options.why: A fair test comes after the research in time. Random days let each test day's neighbours inform the rule.

options.text: It holds out 252 days too few
options.why: 20% of 1,260 is 252: the count is fine.

feedback.correct: The held-out period goes at the end.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Think about what the rule reads on a test day.

explain.text: A 2-day lookback on a test day reads research days around it, and research days read test days. Only a block at the end is after everything research saw (validation, shuffling lies).

items.prose: A held-out year shows Sharpe −0.3 for the chosen rule. The researcher tries a 10-day threshold, sees 0.9 on the same year, and reports 0.9.
items.question: How should the 0.9 be labelled in the note?

options.text: As a research number: the held-out year chose the threshold
As the held-out result
options.why: It was chosen after looking at that year. That makes it research.

options.text: As the average of the two looks, 0.3
options.why: Averaging does not undo the choice. Both looks are now research.

feedback.correct: A second look turns a test into research.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. What chose the threshold?

explain.text: The threshold was picked because of its held-out score, so the year is spent. The note reports −0.3 as the held-out result, and 0.9 as an idea to test on new data.

items.prose: A rule is always in the market, with equal-sized daily gains and losses. It is right on 55% of days.
items.question: What is its annualised Sharpe? Use $\sqrt{252}\,(2p - 1)/\sqrt{1 - (2p - 1)^2}$ and give 2 decimal places.

byKey.noroot: You multiplied by 252, not its square root.

explain.text: $\sqrt{252} \times 0.10/\sqrt{0.99} = 1.60$. Being right 55% of days is already rare; 57% is what a Sharpe of 2 needs.

items.prose: An engine passes the look-ahead check at five cuts and shows Sharpe 1.4. Its `cost` column sums to −0.42.
items.question: What do you conclude?

options.text: Costs are credited, not charged: the 1.4 is inflated
It passed the check at five cuts, so it is honest
options.why: The check sees only future data. A cost with the wrong sign uses none.

options.text: It earns exchange rebates, so negative costs are fine
options.why: A daily rule crossing the spread pays costs. Rebates need a stated model, not a sign error.

options.text: Run more cuts to be sure
options.why: More cuts cannot find a bug that reads no future row.

feedback.correct: One test, one kind of bug.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. What sign should total costs have?

explain.text: Costs shrink the book, so their total must be positive. A negative total adds the cost to every trade. Only the cost check finds it; the look-ahead check cannot.

items.prose: A search tries 10 settings whose research Sharpes have sd 0.4. The best of 10 standard normals averages 1.539.
items.question: What is the expected best under no edge? Give 2 decimal places.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Scale 1.539 by the sd.

byKey.unscaled: Multiply by the sd of the trials, 0.4.

explain.text: $0.4 \times 1.539 = 0.62$. A best of 0.6 from this search is what noise gives.

items.prose: Our real grid: 48 settings, sd 0.451, best 0.72. The note shows only the 8 lookbacks, a corner of the 48, with sd 0.345 and best 0.55. The best of 8 standard normals averages 1.42 (simulated); of 48, 2.24.
items.question: Which verdict is honest?

options.text: Not above noise: the search was 48 settings, and 0.72 is below 1.01
Above noise: 0.55 beats the bar for 8, 0.49
options.why: That counts only the reported corner. The other 40 settings were tries on the same data.

options.text: Above noise, since one of the two checks passes
options.why: A check you can pass by choosing $N$ is no check. Use every setting tried.

feedback.correct: $N$ counts every setting run on the data.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. How many settings were run on these research years?

explain.text: All 48 settings ran on the same research years, so $N = 48$ and the bar is $2.24 \times 0.451 = 1.01$. The 8-lookback view clears 0.49 only because it hides 40 tries.

items.prose: Draft lines for a results note's What failed section.
items.question: Select all that apply: lines that meet the standard.

options.text: The research-best lookback lost money held out: Sharpe −0.45.
Costs of 2.5 bp halved lookback 1's research Sharpe, from 0.84 to 0.46.
The strategy underperformed expectations somewhat.
options.why: Vague: nothing a reader could check.

options.text: 2023 was an unusual year for momentum.
A centred-average version failed the look-ahead check and was removed.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Keep the lines with a number or a named change.

explain.text: Each good line names a result or a change a reader can verify. Vague lines and excuses tell a reviewer nothing, and suggest something is being hidden.

items.prose: After opening the held-out year, you find the engine charged half the intended cost on sells. Settings stay as they were.
items.question: What is the honest way forward?

options.text: Fix the bug, rerun the frozen rule once on the held-out year, and report the bug and both numbers
Fix the bug, choose the lookback again on research, then test on the held-out year
options.why: Re-choosing after seeing the held-out year lets it guide the new choice.

options.text: Keep the old held-out number: the vault is closed
options.why: The old number is known to be wrong. A bug fix with frozen settings is not a new choice, if it is disclosed.

options.text: Fix it quietly and report the new number
options.why: Undisclosed reruns are what a reader cannot check. Say what changed.

feedback.correct: Frozen settings, corrected engine, everything disclosed.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Which option changes no choice and hides nothing?

explain.text: Correcting a cost bug changes how the result is measured, not what was chosen. With the settings frozen, one rerun is defensible if the note lists the bug under What failed. Re-choosing anything would spend the year.
